publication_note: Core: 26 public scenarios across JMeter, k6, Locust and Gatling (104 tasks). Anthropic claude-sonnet-5-5 uses adaptive thinking at high effort; DeepSeek deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-pro and Qwen-Ambassador/Qwen4-Max use thinking-high. All use a 64,000-token output cap and one conditional repair round. Scores are the final answer after the one allowed repair. Costs include all 104 first tries per model and the recorded repair responses (24 for Sonnet, 27 for Flash, 29 for V4 Pro, 16 for Qwen4-Max), estimated from reported token usage at frozen registry prices, not provider invoices. Sonnet was published from Actions run https://github.com/QAInsights/p95-bench/actions/runs/45066297860; both DeepSeek models from https://github.com/QAInsights/p95-bench/actions/runs/45082823742; Qwen4-Max from https://github.com/QAInsights/p95-bench/actions/runs/45113245263 at head 2d6e43f309d0ef51698fee94e503439cdb4b09a6. Qwen ran uncapped via the ModelScope free tier; board costs retain public list prices. Five Qwen first tries ended at the output cap and remain scored as recorded. Flash's Gatling shard uses attempt 2 after an IncompleteRead transport failure in attempt 1; costs cover the merged saved responses.
